commit 3fd0ffaa17c0b2c5ced6ca69ae1dc574bba8e969
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Mon Jun 29 21:34:44 2026 +0800

    feat: rv32 support across run, runtime, and fixtures
    
    andesim now treats rv32 as a first-class peer of rv64, driven by the ELF's
    class byte (e_ident[EI_CLASS]). See docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md.
    
    Run dispatch (driver/):
    - elf_xlen() reads an ELF's width (32/64). fast auto-picks
      qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (explicit --engine wins + warns on a
      conflict); cycle and hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen
      via one shared elf_engine_arch_error -- a clear up-front message instead of
      the engine's cryptic "not of ELFCLASSxx".
    
    Dual-arch runtime (runtime/, config, scripts):
    - runtime/Makefile parameterized by ARCH: rv64 -> build/runtime,
      rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32 (rv32gc/ilp32d, riscv32-unknown-elf-).
    - Real rv64-isms fixed: vplat_syscalls.c L2-cache flush guarded to rv64
      (#if __riscv_xlen==64); handler.c trap CSRs made XLEN-wide, which also fixes
      latent rv64 mepc/mtval truncation and the interrupt-bit test.
    - HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 config var (a second, separate toolchain);
      build_runtime.sh builds both arches (and its stale artifact names fixed);
      build_all.sh runtime delegates to it.
    
    rv32 fixtures (tests/fixtures/):
    - make rv32 -> rv32_spin (asm) + rv32_c_hello (C, links the rv32 runtime),
      reusing existing sources.
    
    Docs: USER_GUIDE sec 1.3 (two toolchains) + new sec 5.1 (rv32 link command and
    the arch-match rules).
    
    Tested (TDD, RED first): elf_xlen unit (driver/elf_syms_test.cpp);
    test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh (both arch directions, incl. a real rv32_c_hello
    run on qemu-system-riscv32); test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh (both runtime
    classes). rv64 fixtures and the fast/cycle/hybrid suites stay green.
    Behavioral change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
+#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
+#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
+#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
+# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
+#
+# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
+# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
+# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
+CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
+CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
+
+[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
+ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
+ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
+if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
+  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
+    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
+      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
+    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
+  fi
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
+fi
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
+
+# rv64 (required).
+if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
+echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
+
+# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
+if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
+  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"

+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
+#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
+#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
+#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
+# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
+#
+# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
+# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
+# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
+CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
+CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
+
+[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
+ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
+ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
+if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
+  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
+    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
+      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
+    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
+  fi
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
+fi
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
+
+# rv64 (required).
+if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
+echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
+
+# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
+if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"

# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).
ARCH ?= rv64

ifeq ($(ARCH),rv64)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
  TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime
else ifeq ($(ARCH),rv32)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32
else
  $(error ARCH must be rv64 or rv32, got '$(ARCH)')
endif

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error No toolchain for ARCH=$(ARCH). Set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (rv64) / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (rv32) in config.env, `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar

# rvNNgc objects link cleanly into rvNNgcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.
CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# gcc adds <-B prefix>/include to the include path, so the two-flag user
# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
	mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	cp $< $@

	rm -rf $(OUT)

Review complete. I read the full diff and the surrounding context of each touched file. Findings below, ordered by value.

## Simplification findings

**1. `driver/cmd_run.cpp:183` - redundant condition in the fast warn guard.**
`if (!cli.engine.empty() && elf_w && elf_w != xlen)` - the `!cli.engine.empty() &&` is logically dead. The top-of-function guard (line 152) limits `cli.engine` to {"", qemu32, qemu64}. When it is empty, `xlen` is set from `elf_w` (so `elf_w != xlen` is false) or `elf_w` is 0 (short-circuits). So `elf_w && elf_w != xlen` already implies an explicit engine.
Simpler: `if (elf_w && elf_w != xlen)`.
Cost: trivial, behavior-identical. (I traced all 6 engine x elf_w cases to confirm.)

**2. `driver/cmd_run.cpp:179-182` - "default then override" restates 64 twice.**
`int xlen = 64;` then `else if (cli.engine == kQemuId64) xlen = 64;`. Each branch is terminal, so a closing `else` reads cleaner than a default that the qemu64 branch re-asserts:
```cpp
int xlen;
if (cli.engine == kQemuId32) xlen = 32;
else if (cli.engine == kQemuId64) xlen = 64;
else xlen = elf_w ? elf_w : 64;   // no explicit engine: follow the ELF
```
Cost: low, optional. Lateral readability gain, not a big win.

**3. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh:13` + `test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh:13` - `cfg_val()` duplicated byte-identically.**
`tests/lib/log.sh` already exists to hold "patterns duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts" (its own words) and both scripts source it. Move `cfg_val` into `log.sh`.
Cost: low. Removes the copy and is the intended home.

**4. `tests/fixtures/Makefile:167-169` and `:142-144` - the rv32 runtime rule duplicates the rv64 rule's prereq list verbatim.**
`$(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h` appears in both grouped-target rules. Extract once: `RUNTIME_DEPS := ...` and use in both. Likewise `VPLAT_RT32` (lines 77-79) mirrors `VPLAT_RT` (57-59) and could derive via `$(patsubst $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/%,$(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/%,$(VPLAT_RT))`.
Cost: low DRY cleanup; the patsubst is arguably less readable, so the prereq-list extraction is the clearer win.

**5. Two scripts repeat the TC32 resolve+skip block** (`arch_match.sh:49`, `runtime_dual.sh:30`, plus the `TC64=...:-$(cfg_val ...)` / `TC32=...` lines). Near-identical except the SKIP message text. A `tc32_or_skip <msg>` helper in `log.sh` would collapse it. Cost: low, optional - the differing message reduces the payoff, so weaker than #3.

## Checked and genuinely clean (no change needed)

- **`driver/cmd_run.cpp:84-94` `elf_engine_arch_error`** - the three early-return guards (`ex==0`, `eng.xlen==0`, `ex==eng.xlen`) are each distinct and necessary, none redundant. `char buf[256]; snprintf; return buf;` is established house style here (identical pattern in `state.hpp:48`, `cmd_doctor.cpp:302`). `%ld` is correct: `eng.xlen` is `long` (`engine_descriptor.hpp:32`). Note only: its sibling guard `hybrid_hw_check` (`hybrid.cpp:46`) builds the same "engine ... is rvNN" message with `+`/`std::to_string` concat - a cosmetic inconsistency, not a defect; both styles are used repo-wide.

- **`runtime/Makefile:27-39` ARCH ifeq** - clean. You asked if the rv32 vars could derive more simply: only `TRIPLE` (`riscv$(ARCH:rv%=%)-unknown-elf`) and `-march=$(ARCH)gc` are regular. `-mabi` (lp64d vs **i**lp32d), `TOOLCHAIN` (two env vars), and `OUT` are irregular and need per-arch literals anyway. For exactly two arches with an `$(error ...)` for bad input, the explicit block is clearer than a half-derived one. Leave it.

- **`runtime/handler.c:34,42,45`** - `1UL << (__riscv_xlen - 1)` and `mcause & ~intbit` are the standard idiom and correct: `unsigned long` is exactly XLEN-wide on both targeted ABIs (32-bit ilp32, 64-bit lp64), so the MSB lands right and no truncation. `_exit((int) mcause)` cast is appropriate. No simpler form.

- **`driver/elf_syms.cpp:124-135` `elf_xlen`** - minimal: reads only `e_ident`, switch on `EI_CLASS`, 0 on any failure. No redundant state.

No dead code or deep nesting introduced anywhere in the diff. The only behavior-identical redundancy worth fixing is #1; the rest are low-cost DRY tidy-ups.
